 Advertisement Maine gubernatorial election results: Bennett, Charles and Pingree vie for governor's office
 The polls close at 8 p.m.
 Advertisement Russ Reed Maine gubernatorial election results: Bennett, Charles and Pingree vie for governor's office
 The polls close at 8 p.m.
 Russ Reed FULL RESULTS: SENATE | 1ST DISTRICT | 2ND DISTRICT | MAINE LEGISLATURE | ANDROSCOGGIN COUNTY | CUMBERLAND COUNTY | FRANKLIN COUNTY | KENNEBEC COUNTY | KNOX COUNTY | LINCOLN COUNTY | OXFORD COUNTY | SAGADAHOC COUNTY | WALDO COUNTY | YORK COUNTY | NEW HAMPSHIRE'S MAJOR RACES 
 Gov. Janet Mills is in the final year of her second straight term and under Maine law, no governor can serve three consecutive terms.
 Advertisement Hannah Pingree, the former Speaker of the Maine House of Representatives and a former member of the Mills administration, won the Democratic primary after a ranked-choice voting tabulation involving five candidates.
 Bobby Charles, a former U.S. assistant secretary of state, won the Republican primary after a ranked-choice voting tabulation involving eight candidates.
 State Sen. Rick Bennett, an independent candidate, qualified to appear on the general election ballot.
 There are also two declared write-in candidates in the race: independent John Glowa Sr. and Republican Randy Wilcox.
 Learn more about each of the three candidates who qualified for the general election ballot below. The candidates are listed in alphabetical order.
 Rick Bennett
 Bennett has been involved in Maine politics since 1990, when he was elected to the Maine House of Representatives. He was then elected to the State Senate in 1996 and served the maximum of four consecutive two-year terms, including a stint as Senate president (2001-02).
 After terming out of the Maine Senate in 2004, Bennett remained in the private sector for 16 years and served as chair of the Maine Republican Party from July 2013 to January 2017. He was reelected to the State Senate in 2020 and currently serves District 18 in Oxford County.
Bennett announced in June 2025 that he was unenrolling from the GOP to run for governor as an independent.
 "I was reluctant to do it because I do want things to work, and I believe that parties had a place. What I've come to conclude is parties have become a net negative in our political discourse," Bennett said in an interview with Maine's Total Coverage . "They actually keep us fighting with each other, hating on each other, afraid of each other, and that is the operating role of a party these days."
 Bennett said he wants to reduce down payments for first-time homebuyers by having the state back part of the traditional 20% down payment, and he also wants to build more housing. The son of a teacher, Bennett said he wants to appoint a Department of Education Commissioner who will work on improving students' reading proficiency.
 The independent candidate hopes Mainers put party affiliation aside when they head to the polls.
 "I love this state. My family's been here for ten generations plus. I'm a lifelong Mainer, and Maine people deserve a functioning government and a governor who will put them first, not the political parties," Bennett said.
 Bobby Charles
 Charles led the Republican primary by 17 points after all of the ballots were tallied on Election Night. But with a crowded field of candidates, he only received 37.9% of the vote, necessitating a ranked-choice tabulation.
 "I asked my team to look at all the jurisdictions that have ever done ranked-choice, including in Europe, and there was no jurisdiction where someone had been up in a field of eight, or even like that, by 17 or 18 points and didn't prevail," Charles said in an interview with Maine's Total Coverage .
 Charles worked in the federal government as the Assistant Secretary of State for International Narcotics and Law Enforcement Affairs under Secretaries Colin Powell and Condoleezza Rice during the George W. Bush administration. Charles spent many years working to combat illegal drug problems in the United States.
 His campaign slogan is "cut crime, cut taxes, no nonsense." Charles has what he calls a 20-point accountability plan that will do things like enforce strict criminal accountability.
 When it comes to taxes, Charles said he would raise the homestead exemption from its current level of $25,000 to $50,000 in his first two-year budget before raising it to $100,000 in his second biennium. He also want to eliminate the state income tax, saying it will put more money in people's pockets.
 "Ronald Reagan, for whom I worked, cut the income tax at the federal level by 25% and immediately generated 18 million jobs," Charles said.
 Charles previously served as the Office of Domestic Policy's deputy associate director from 1992-1993 during the George H.W. Bush administration, as well as a temporary appointee during President Ronald Reagan's first term in the White House during three stretches between 1981 and 1983. From 1995-99, Charles served as staff director and chief council for the National Security, International Affairs, and Criminal Justice Subcommittee in the U.S. House of Representatives.
 Hannah Pingree
 Pingree was second in the Democratic primary behind Dr. Nirav Shah after first-choice votes were counted, four of the five candidates on the ballot earned at least 20% of the first-choice votes. After the ranked-choice voting tabulation was conducted, Pingree finished ahead of Shah, the former director of the Maine CDC.
 "I think ranked choice was a very positive process," Pingree said in an interview with Maine's Total Coverage . "It ended up being a race where we talked about the issues. There were not a lot of negative attacks. And after the race was over, all four of my primary opponents have supported me. They've been helping me in my campaign."
 Pingree served in the Maine House of Representatives from 2002 to 2010, including as House Majority Leader from 2006 to 2008 and Speaker of the House from 2008 to 2010.
 She recently spent six years in the administration of Gov. Janet Mills, working as the director of the Office of Policy Innovation and the Future. Pingree tackled issues like housing and the environment, and was on the front lines of the 2024 winter storms that devastated parts of Maine's coast.
 "I am different than Governor Mills. I'm appreciative of some of the issues that I've been able to work on, but I won't govern in the same way she has," Pingree said.
 Pingree said she wants to implement the "science of reading" in Maine, as well as universal pre-K and other education policies that have worked well in other parts of the country.
 When it comes to housing, Pingree said she wants to get every homeless veteran off the street and cut red tape so projects can get off the ground faster. She also wants to invest $100 million a year in housing.
 Pingree, the daughter of U.S. Rep. Chellie Pingree, is seeking to become the youngest female governor in Maine history.
